Smile Montana Scholarship

[excluded contact/navigation scope]

Thank you for applying for our scholarship! Please read the details and instructions of this application carefully before submitting.
Details:
1. One $1,000.00 scholarship will be awarded to a student in each of the following high schools; Columbia Falls, Whitefish, Glacier, Flathead, Bigfork and Eureka.
2. Selection of scholarship recipient is based on quality of essay first and then other information provided is considered. Grammar and structure of essay is important, but making us smile is most important.
3. Applicant must be a graduating senior planning to attend a post-secondary      institution in 2026.
4. Application must be submitted by April 1, 2026. Physical copies can be returned to school counselor or a digital copy can be emailed to [contact omitted]. Digital files should be a single PDF including all required documents. Please do not send word files, google doc links or multiple files.
Instructions
Fill out personal information page
Include 1-2 page typed essay answering the following prompt:
Share a personal story that will make us smile (or laugh!)
Provide recent school transcript

# THE RIPPLE EFFECT SCHOLARSHIP APPLICATION PROCESS

The scholarship is available to any Whitefish or Columbia Falls senior entering a two- or four-year college
program with plans to major in an environmental science field.  Appropriate courses of study for
consideration in the scholarship program include: biology, ecology, environmental science/studies,
hydrology, or other fields related to water quality as approved by WLI staff. To qualify, students must also
have a 3.0 minimum grade point average.

*Scholarship amount is $500*

## Scholarship Applicant Responsibilities

In addition to completing a Scholarship Application Form (attached below), students must submit:

-Transcripts

-A 300-500 word essay describing your “watershed ethic.” In short, what is your philosophy
regarding human activities that affect water quality? How does your watershed ethic make you a
good steward of water resources?

-Email and phone numbers of TWO teachers to be used for references.

## Deadlines

• Completed applications and attached documentation for the **College Scholarship** must be postmarked
by **April 15th** and delivered to the Whitefish Lake Institute to be considered.

All scholarship recipients will be required to complete and submit to WLI by September 1<sup>st</sup> a Scholarship
Recipient Form requiring your Social Security Number (for proper accounting and tax records), the full
name and mailing address for the college you’ll be attending, and the semester in which funds will be used.
Funds will be sent directly to the college.

## Important Dates

April 15<sup>th</sup> Completed College Scholarship Application with Required Materials Postmarked for delivery
to WLI

May 1<sup>st</sup> Scholarships awarded

September 1<sup>st</sup> Scholarship Recipient Form Postmarked for delivery to WLI (Student will receive form upon
being awarded scholarship).

# THE RIPPLE EFFECT SCHOLARSHIP APPLICATION PROCESS

The scholarship is available to any Whitefish or Columbia Falls senior entering a two- or four-year college
program with plans to major in an environmental science field.  Appropriate courses of study for
consideration in the scholarship program include: biology, ecology, environmental science/studies,
hydrology, or other fields related to water quality as approved by WLI staff. To qualify, students must also
have a 3.0 minimum grade point average.

*Scholarship amount is $500*

## Scholarship Applicant Responsibilities

In addition to completing a Scholarship Application Form (attached below), students must submit:

-Transcripts

-A 300-500 word essay describing your “watershed ethic.” In short, what is your philosophy
regarding human activities that affect water quality? How does your watershed ethic make you a
good steward of water resources?

-Email and phone numbers of TWO teachers to be used for references.

## Deadlines

• Completed applications and attached documentation for the **College Scholarship** must be postmarked
by **April 15th** and delivered to the Whitefish Lake Institute to be considered.

All scholarship recipients will be required to complete and submit to WLI by September 1<sup>st</sup> a Scholarship
Recipient Form requiring your Social Security Number (for proper accounting and tax records), the full
name and mailing address for the college you’ll be attending, and the semester in which funds will be used.
Funds will be sent directly to the college.

## Important Dates

April 15<sup>th</sup> Completed College Scholarship Application with Required Materials Postmarked for delivery
to WLI

May 1<sup>st</sup> Scholarships awarded

September 1<sup>st</sup> Scholarship Recipient Form Postmarked for delivery to WLI (Student will receive form upon
being awarded scholarship).

**INCOMPLETE APPLICATIONS WILL NOT BE CONSIDERED**
Deadline: April 17th 2026
Amount of Award: Undetermined

WHITEFISH ROTARY SCHOLARSHIP
The Whitefish Rotary Club will award scholarships to graduating seniors from Whitefish High School.  The number and dollar amount of scholarships awarded will depend on the number of quality applications received and approved but will be a minimum of $1000 per scholarship.  Scholarships from Whitefish Rotary Club may be used for any higher education pursuit: 2yr programs, 4yr programs, trade and vocational schools.
To be considered, an applicant will need to meet the following criteria:
Attend Whitefish High School for the entirety of their senior year and graduate from Whitefish High School.  (Gap year applicants accepted).
Be accepted to and plan to attend a Vocational Tech Institution, Community College, College/University, or a Trade-School Program.  (Gap year applicants accepted but must provide confirmation of approval of gap year).
Attend the Whitefish High School Awards Ceremony – a representative from Whitefish Rotary will be present to award the scholarship.
Attend a Whitefish Rotary regular lunch meeting to formally be recognized by our club, tell our club where you plan to attend in your pursuit of higher education, the program or degree you are interested in studying, and accept the scholarship.
The scholarship will be paid in one installment of $1000 or two installments of $500 per semester.
The scholarship funds will be made payable to the institution or program you are registered for and sent to the institution by our Treasurer (so please provide the appropriate information prior to your first semester or when you receive the bill for tuition).  The funds are to be credited to the student’s account for payment of tuition or other applicable higher education expenses.  In the event the scholarship money provided by Whitefish Rotary is not immediately needed because of other scholarships or financial benefits received, the scholarship money will be held for up to 2 years by our club and it is your responsibility to notify Whitefish Rotary when the scholarship money is needed at that time.
Application and listed requirements are to be completed and returned to:
Whitefish High School Guidance office by:  3:30pm on April 17, 2026

# <PRIVATE_PERSON> Aviation Excellence Award

# Application Information

The General Aviation Manufacturers Association (GAMA) is an international trade association
dedicated to fostering and advancing the general welfare, safety, interests, and activities of the
global business and general aviation industry. GAMA represents over 140 of the world’s leading
manufacturers of general aviation aircraft, engines, avionics, and components, as well as
operators of maintenance facilities, fixed base operations, aircraft fleets, and pilot and training
facilities. GAMA offers the <PRIVATE_PERSON> Aviation Excellence Award annually as part of
its commitment to advancing careers in general aviation.

## Eligibility Criteria

## An applicant must:

1. Be a current student at a U.S. high school, graduating in the Spring of 2026;

2. Be accepted to and enrolling in an institution for an aviation-related degree program (*e.g.,*
flight training, aviation management, aerospace engineering, aviation maintenance); and

3. Have a 3.0 or better grade point average (on a 4.0 scale).

## Application Contents

1. Application form

2. Essay question response

3. Current high school transcript

4. Letter(s) of recommendation (maximum two)

Applicants will be assessed on their academic achievements, involvement in extra-curricular
activities, and their essay question responses.

Send completed application packages to (electronic submissions preferred):

<u>[contact omitted]</u> or Attn: <PRIVATE_PERSON> Scholarship

General Aviation Manufacturers Associations
[excluded contact/navigation scope]

[excluded contact/navigation scope]

**Completed applications must be received by GAMA by April 24, 2026.** Two winners will be
chosen annually to receive a $2,000 USD award. GAMA will notify the winner by email.

are you interested in a career in general aviation, and how do you plan to pursue it?

# <PRIVATE_PERSON> Aviation Excellence Award

# Application Information

The General Aviation Manufacturers Association (GAMA) is an international trade association
dedicated to fostering and advancing the general welfare, safety, interests, and activities of the
global business and general aviation industry. GAMA represents over 140 of the world’s leading
manufacturers of general aviation aircraft, engines, avionics, and components, as well as
operators of maintenance facilities, fixed base operations, aircraft fleets, and pilot and training
facilities. GAMA offers the <PRIVATE_PERSON> Aviation Excellence Award annually as part of
its commitment to advancing careers in general aviation.

## Eligibility Criteria

## An applicant must:

1. Be a current student at a U.S. high school, graduating in the Spring of 2026;

2. Be accepted to and enrolling in an institution for an aviation-related degree program (*e.g.,*
flight training, aviation management, aerospace engineering, aviation maintenance); and

3. Have a 3.0 or better grade point average (on a 4.0 scale).

## Application Contents

1. Application form

4. Letter(s) of recommendation (maximum two)

Applicants will be assessed on their academic achievements, involvement in extra-curricular
activities, and their essay question responses.

## Eligible Student

Graduating High School Seniors

## Application Open

Thursday, January 01, 2026

## Deadline Date

Thursday, April 30, 2026




#### Required Criteria

The following are required criteria for this scholarship. Applicants _**must**_:

- be a member of the Order of the Rainbow for Girls.
- be a graduating high school senior from a Montana high school.
- demonstrate a high school GPA of 2.0 or higher
- plan to be enrolled in a degree program in an accredited post-secondary educational institution (university, college, community college, college of technology, or technical school).

Selection is based on the following factors: financial need, participation in school, community, and church activities, long-term goals, and motivation.

#### Reapplication

Previous recipients are NOT allowed to apply again.

## Awards

This scholarship typically provides the following each academic year.

#### Award Type

One-Time

#### Amount per Award

Typically **$3,000** per academic year.

#### \\# of Awards

Typically **1 to 2** recipients each year.

## Applying

#### Application Access Code

### 25EJMS

Use this Access Code to apply directly for this scholarship within the [MCF Scholarship Portal](https://www.grantinterface.com/Home/Logon?urlkey=mtcfscholarship).

#### Materials Needed

The following materials are required for submission with an application.

- Most Recent Transcript (High School)
- FAFSA FSS

# National Aviation Explorer Scholarships Guide and Application

The National Aviation Exploring Committee awards scholarships to recognize
excellence among Aviation Explorers studying the technologies and the skills
needed in the field of aviation. The sponsors that provide the scholarships are
committed to aviation's future leadership. Applicant's description of their personal
record should show that they can successfully complete the aviation career
educational activity for which they are requesting the scholarship. Also their
personal record should show their involvement in life skills, citizenship, leadership,
and character education experiences that add to the quality of life.

NOTE: If scholarship funds are used for training in the avionics, pilot, maintenance,
or management categories, the flight training must be provided by the FAA
Approved Part 141 and Part 61 school or through an accredited college or university
in pursuit of a degree leading to an aviation profession.

---

##### Background

The National Aviation Exploring Committee awards scholarships annually to
encourage Aviation Explorers to enter and complete an aviation curriculum.
National Aviation Committee Members know that aviation offers a variety of
exciting, well-paying careers, and that qualified and motivated Aviation Explorers

should be given encouragement and assistance in choosing a career in aviation. Through the years,
the National Aviation Exploring Committee has been a supporter of projects designed to promote
aviation to young people. This long standing dedication to the Aviation Exploring community
continues with the National Aviation Explorer Scholarship Program.

##### Applicant Eligibility and Checklist P

1. Applicant must be currently registered and active in an Aviation Explorer post.

2. Applicant must obtain parent or guardian signature on the application if under 18 years of
age.

3. Applicant must provide a minimum of three recommendation letters from an aviation post
advisor, aviation professional, teacher, employer, or community leaders. Recommendation
letters should not come from family members.

4. Attach the following items in .pdf format in an email to <u>[contact omitted]</u> by the deadline:

a. Completed application

b. High resolution self portrait

c. Letter(s) of recommendation

d. Copy of any FAA written exam results

e. FAA medical, if applicable

f. Other FAA certificates, if any

g. College transcript, if applicable

#### NOTE: All components must be submitted in the same email. Components submitted in separate emails will not be accepted.

##### How to Apply

An Aviation Explorer can apply for either of the two National Aviation Explorer scholarships for $2,500.00 by
submitting one standard application and other requested documentation by the deadline noted below.
Aviation Explorer Scholarship recipients will be selected by members of the National Aviation Exploring
Committee and will be notified by email no later than July 1<sup>st</sup> annually. Since applications are not carried
over year to year, previous applications can be updated and resubmitted to the local council.

##### Deadlines

| April 30 | Aviation Explorer submits completed application, 3 letters of recommendation and high-resolution photo to National Exploring Service Center via email, [contact omitted]. |
| --- | --- |

July1 Applicants will receive notice of award via email.

---

# SELECT THE SCHOLARSHIPS FOR WHICH YOU'D LIKE TO APPLY:

Please read the scholarship criteria carefully to be sure you are eligible.

The National Aviation Exploring Committee awards individual scholarships of $2,500 annually to
Aviation Explorers pursuing an interest in aviation. The intent of these scholarships is to identify
and reward those individuals who best exemplify the qualities that lead to success in the aviation
industry.

You may apply for as many types of scholarships as you wish. However, you are only eligible to
receive one scholarship per academic year. Candidates are judged on their documentation of
leadership involvement, aviation accomplishments, and recognition of achievement as well as the
strength of their essay stating their educational plan for a career in aviation.

Note that there are time limitations for receiving scholarship funds.

**Degree Leading to an Aviation Profession** (Scholarship value $2,500.00,) Awarded to an
Aviation Explorer accepted or attending an accredited college or university in pursuit of a
degree leading to an aviation profession. Provide a copy of your high school or college
transcript. Funds must be redeemed within four years of receiving the award.

##### Avionics (Scholarship value $2,500.00)

Awarded to Aviation Explorer high school seniors or college students who plan to or are
attending an accredited school in an avionics program. Funds must be redeemed within two
years of receiving the award.

##### Pilot (Pilot Certificate) (Scholarship value $2,500.00)

Awarded to an Aviation Explorer pursuing their sport or private pilot certificate (any type
aircraft) and may or may not be pursuing a career in aviation. Flight training must be
completed within one year. Candidates are judged on the strength of their essay stating their
plan for their pilot's license, evidence of interest in learning to fly, and performance history
in education and/or work, volunteerism, financial need. Funds must be redeemed within two
years of receiving the award.

##### Maintenance (Scholarship value $2,500.00)

Awarded to Aviation Explorer high school seniors or college students who plan to or are
attending an accredited school in an aircraft repair program. Funds must be redeemed
within two years of receiving the award.

##### Management (Scholarship value $2,500.00)

Awarded to an Aviation Explorer student in an aviation management program (to include
design, engineering, airport management, etc.) at an accredited college or university. Funds
must be redeemed within two years of receiving the award.

---

## APPLICANT'S PERSONAL RECORD

Attach additional sheets as needed.

1. <u>CAREER OPPORTUNITIES EXPERIENCE</u> Describe your aviation career goals to include how you
can successfully complete the aviation career educational activity for which you are requesting the
scholarship.

2. <u>LIFE SKILLS EXPERIENCE</u> Describe your accomplishments/involvement with aviation to include
activities that provided positive social interaction.

3. <u>CITIZENSHIP EXPERIENCE</u> List all organizations that you were a member of during high school
[excluded contact/navigation scope]
those in which you are now active.

---

4. <u>LEADERSHIP EXPERIENCE</u> List all leadership positions that you have held during
high school and college. Indicate with an asterisk[*] those positions now held.

5. <u>CHARACTER EDUCATION EXPERiENCE</u> List important achievements, awards, or recognitions
that you have received; the organizations that presented them; and the year received.

6. <u>OPTIONAL ADDITIONAL INFORMATION</u> Provide any additional information that you feel
important such as work experience, personal hardships, what you have learned from volunteer
experiences, unusual financial circumstances, etc.

---

7. <u>EDUCATIONAL PLAN</u> Submit a 500 word educational plan showing how
you are going to finance your goal for a career in aviation.

# National Aviation Explorer Scholarships Guide and Application

The National Aviation Exploring Committee awards scholarships to recognize
excellence among Aviation Explorers studying the technologies and the skills
needed in the field of aviation. The sponsors that provide the scholarships are
committed to aviation's future leadership. Applicant's description of their personal
record should show that they can successfully complete the aviation career
educational activity for which they are requesting the scholarship. Also their
personal record should show their involvement in life skills, citizenship, leadership,
and character education experiences that add to the quality of life.

NOTE: If scholarship funds are used for training in the avionics, pilot, maintenance,
or management categories, the flight training must be provided by the FAA
Approved Part 141 and Part 61 school or through an accredited college or university
in pursuit of a degree leading to an aviation profession.

---

##### Background

The National Aviation Exploring Committee awards scholarships annually to
encourage Aviation Explorers to enter and complete an aviation curriculum.
National Aviation Committee Members know that aviation offers a variety of
exciting, well-paying careers, and that qualified and motivated Aviation Explorers

should be given encouragement and assistance in choosing a career in aviation. Through the years,
the National Aviation Exploring Committee has been a supporter of projects designed to promote
aviation to young people. This long standing dedication to the Aviation Exploring community
continues with the National Aviation Explorer Scholarship Program.

##### Applicant Eligibility and Checklist P

1. Applicant must be currently registered and active in an Aviation Explorer post.

2. Applicant must obtain parent or guardian signature on the application if under 18 years of
age.

3. Applicant must provide a minimum of three recommendation letters from an aviation post
advisor, aviation professional, teacher, employer, or community leaders. Recommendation
letters should not come from family members.

4. Attach the following items in .pdf format in an email to <u>[contact omitted]</u> by the deadline:

a. Completed application

b. High resolution self portrait

c. Letter(s) of recommendation

d. Copy of any FAA written exam results

e. FAA medical, if applicable

f. Other FAA certificates, if any

g. College transcript, if applicable

#### NOTE: All components must be submitted in the same email. Components submitted in separate emails will not be accepted.

##### How to Apply

An Aviation Explorer can apply for either of the two National Aviation Explorer scholarships for $2,500.00 by
submitting one standard application and other requested documentation by the deadline noted below.
Aviation Explorer Scholarship recipients will be selected by members of the National Aviation Exploring
Committee and will be notified by email no later than July 1<sup>st</sup> annually. Since applications are not carried
over year to year, previous applications can be updated and resubmitted to the local council.

##### Deadlines

| April 30 | Aviation Explorer submits completed application, 3 letters of recommendation and high-resolution photo to National Exploring Service Center via email, [contact omitted]. |
| --- | --- |

July1 Applicants will receive notice of award via email.

---

# SELECT THE SCHOLARSHIPS FOR WHICH YOU'D LIKE TO APPLY:

Please read the scholarship criteria carefully to be sure you are eligible.

The National Aviation Exploring Committee awards individual scholarships of $2,500 annually to
Aviation Explorers pursuing an interest in aviation. The intent of these scholarships is to identify
and reward those individuals who best exemplify the qualities that lead to success in the aviation
industry.

You may apply for as many types of scholarships as you wish. However, you are only eligible to
receive one scholarship per academic year. Candidates are judged on their documentation of
leadership involvement, aviation accomplishments, and recognition of achievement as well as the
strength of their essay stating their educational plan for a career in aviation.

Note that there are time limitations for receiving scholarship funds.

**Degree Leading to an Aviation Profession** (Scholarship value $2,500.00,) Awarded to an
Aviation Explorer accepted or attending an accredited college or university in pursuit of a
degree leading to an aviation profession. Provide a copy of your high school or college
transcript. Funds must be redeemed within four years of receiving the award.

##### Avionics (Scholarship value $2,500.00)

Awarded to Aviation Explorer high school seniors or college students who plan to or are
attending an accredited school in an avionics program. Funds must be redeemed within two
years of receiving the award.

##### Pilot (Pilot Certificate) (Scholarship value $2,500.00)

Awarded to an Aviation Explorer pursuing their sport or private pilot certificate (any type
aircraft) and may or may not be pursuing a career in aviation. Flight training must be
completed within one year. Candidates are judged on the strength of their essay stating their
plan for their pilot's license, evidence of interest in learning to fly, and performance history
in education and/or work, volunteerism, financial need. Funds must be redeemed within two
years of receiving the award.

##### Maintenance (Scholarship value $2,500.00)

Awarded to Aviation Explorer high school seniors or college students who plan to or are
attending an accredited school in an aircraft repair program. Funds must be redeemed
within two years of receiving the award.

##### Management (Scholarship value $2,500.00)

Awarded to an Aviation Explorer student in an aviation management program (to include
design, engineering, airport management, etc.) at an accredited college or university. Funds
must be redeemed within two years of receiving the award.

---

## APPLICANT'S PERSONAL RECORD

Attach additional sheets as needed.

1. <u>CAREER OPPORTUNITIES EXPERIENCE</u> Describe your aviation career goals to include how you
can successfully complete the aviation career educational activity for which you are requesting the
scholarship.

2. <u>LIFE SKILLS EXPERIENCE</u> Describe your accomplishments/involvement with aviation to include
activities that provided positive social interaction.

3. <u>CITIZENSHIP EXPERIENCE</u> List all organizations that you were a member of during high school
[excluded contact/navigation scope]
those in which you are now active.

---

4. <u>LEADERSHIP EXPERIENCE</u> List all leadership positions that you have held during
high school and college. Indicate with an asterisk[*] those positions now held.

5. <u>CHARACTER EDUCATION EXPERiENCE</u> List important achievements, awards, or recognitions
that you have received; the organizations that presented them; and the year received.

6. <u>OPTIONAL ADDITIONAL INFORMATION</u> Provide any additional information that you feel
important such as work experience, personal hardships, what you have learned from volunteer
experiences, unusual financial circumstances, etc.

---

7. <u>EDUCATIONAL PLAN</u> Submit a 500 word educational plan showing how
you are going to finance your goal for a career in aviation.

evidence.excerpt:
# National Aviation Explorer Scholarships Guide and Application

The National Aviation Exploring Committee awards scholarships to recognize
excellence among Aviation Explorers studying the technologies and the skills
needed in the field of aviation. The sponsors that provide the scholarships are
committed to aviation's future leadership. Applicant's description of their personal
record should show that they can successfully complete the aviation career
educational activity for which they are requesting the scholarship. Also their
personal record should show their involvement in life skills, citizenship, leadership,
and character education experiences that add to the quality of life.

NOTE: If scholarship funds are used for training in the avionics, pilot, maintenance,
or management categories, the flight training must be provided by the FAA
Approved Part 141 and Part 61 school or through an accredited college or university
in pursuit of a degree leading to an aviation profession.

---

##### Background

The National Aviation Exploring Committee awards scholarships annually to
encourage Aviation Explorers to enter and complete an aviation curriculum.
National Aviation Committee Members know that aviation offers a variety of
exciting, well-paying careers, and that qualified and motivated Aviation Explorers

should be given encouragement and assistance in choosing a career in aviation. Through the years,
the National Aviation Exploring Committee has been a supporter of projects designed to promote
aviation to young people. This long standing dedication to the Aviation Exploring community
continues with the National Aviation Explorer Scholarship Program.

##### Applicant Eligibility and Checklist P

1. Applicant must be currently registered and active in an Aviation Explorer post.

2. Applicant must obtain parent or guardian signature on the application if under 18 years of
age.

3. Applicant must provide a minimum of three recommendation letters from an aviation post
advisor, aviation professional, teacher, employer, or community leaders. Recommendation
letters should not come from family members.

4. Attach the following items in .pdf format in an email to <u>[contact omitted]</u> by the deadline:

a. Completed application

b. High resolution self portrait

c. Letter(s) of recommendation

d. Copy of any FAA written exam results

e. FAA medical, if applicable

f. Other FAA certificates, if any

g. College transcript, if applicable

#### NOTE: All components must be submitted in the same email. Components submitted in separate emails will not be accepted.

##### How to Apply

An Aviation Explorer can apply for either of the two National Aviation Explorer scholarships for $2,500.00 by
submitting one standard application and other requested documentation by the deadline noted below.
Aviation Explorer Scholarship recipients will be selected by members of the National Aviation Exploring
Committee and will be notified by email no later than July 1<sup>st</sup> annually. Since applications are not carried
over year to year, previous applications can be updated and resubmitted to the local council.

##### Deadlines

| April 30 | Aviation Explorer submits completed application, 3 letters of recommendation and high-resolution photo to National Exploring Service Center via email, [contact omitted]. |
| --- | --- |

July1 Applicants will receive notice of award via email.

---

# SELECT THE SCHOLARSHIPS FOR WHICH YOU'D LIKE TO APPLY:

Please read the scholarship criteria carefully to be sure you are eligible.

The National Aviation Exploring Committee awards individual scholarships of $2,500 annually to
Aviation Explorers pursuing an interest in aviation. The intent of these scholarships is to identify
and reward those individuals who best exemplify the qualities that lead to success in the aviation
industry.

You may apply for as many types of scholarships as you wish. However, you are only eligible to
receive one scholarship per academic year. Candidates are judged on their documentation of
leadership involvement, aviation accomplishments, and recognition of achievement as well as the
strength of their essay stating their educational plan for a career in aviation.

Note that there are time limitations for receiving scholarship funds.

**Degree Leading to an Aviation Profession** (Scholarship value $2,500.00,) Awarded to an
Aviation Explorer accepted or attending an accredited college or university in pursuit of a
degree leading to an aviation profession. Provide a copy of your high school or college
transcript. Funds must be redeemed within four years of receiving the award.

##### Avionics (Scholarship value $2,500.00)

Awarded to Aviation Explorer high school seniors or college students who plan to or are
attending an accredited school in an avionics program. Funds must be redeemed within two
years of receiving the award.

##### Pilot (Pilot Certificate) (Scholarship value $2,500.00)

Awarded to an Aviation Explorer pursuing their sport or private pilot certificate (any type
aircraft) and may or may not be pursuing a career in aviation. Flight training must be
completed within one year. Candidates are judged on the strength of their essay stating their
plan for their pilot's license, evidence of interest in learning to fly, and performance history
in education and/or work, volunteerism, financial need. Funds must be redeemed within two
years of receiving the award.

##### Maintenance (Scholarship value $2,500.00)

Awarded to Aviation Explorer high school seniors or college students who plan to or are
attending an accredited school in an aircraft repair program. Funds must be redeemed
within two years of receiving the award.

##### Management (Scholarship value $2,500.00)

Awarded to an Aviation Explorer student in an aviation management program (to include
design, engineering, airport management, etc.) at an accredited college or university. Funds
must be redeemed within two years of receiving the award.

---

## APPLICANT'S PERSONAL RECORD

Attach additional sheets as needed.

1. <u>CAREER OPPORTUNITIES EXPERIENCE</u> Describe your aviation career goals to include how you
can successfully complete the aviation career educational activity for which you are requesting the
scholarship.

2. <u>LIFE SKILLS EXPERIENCE</u> Describe your accomplishments/involvement with aviation to include
activities that provided positive social interaction.

3. <u>CITIZENSHIP EXPERIENCE</u> List all organizations that you were a member of during high school
[excluded contact/navigation scope]
those in which you are now active.

---

4. <u>LEADERSHIP EXPERIENCE</u> List all leadership positions that you have held during
high school and college. Indicate with an asterisk[*] those positions now held.

5. <u>CHARACTER EDUCATION EXPERiENCE</u> List important achievements, awards, or recognitions
that you have received; the organizations that presented them; and the year received.

6. <u>OPTIONAL ADDITIONAL INFORMATION</u> Provide any additional information that you feel
important such as work experience, personal hardships, what you have learned from volunteer
experiences, unusual financial circumstances, etc.

---

7. <u>EDUCATIONAL PLAN</u> Submit a 500 word educational plan showing how
you are going to finance your goal for a career in aviation.

# Character Counts! Scholarship

![](https://bigskygames.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Pye-Barker-logo-standard-1024x238.png)

## About the Scholarship

### 2027 Scholarship Deadline: Friday, May 1

The Big Sky State Games has teamed up with the CHARACTER COUNTS! Coalition and Pye-Barker Fire & Safety to recognize the importance of sportsmanship and character in Montana student athletes. CHARACTER COUNTS! is a nonprofit organization striving to improve the character of today’s youth. It is based on common ethical values that transcend political, religious, socio-economic, and cultural differences. Called the “Six Pillars of Character,” these values are: trustworthiness, respect, responsibility, fairness, caring and citizenship. Character Counts! Scholarship is sponsored by Pye-Barker Fire & Safety.

Over the past twenty-seven years, the Big Sky State Games has awarded the Character Counts! Scholarship to outstanding Montana female and male student-citizen-athletes involved in the Big Sky State Games. The scholarship can be used for any secondary education after high school. This includes trade schools and community colleges.

Only high school juniors during the 2026-2027 school year are eligible for this scholarship. This is to ensure that fellow students can observe the scholarship winners during their senior year and to recognize the traits the students show. You can fill out the application below. It will also be available at all Montana High Schools Guidance Counselor offices.

[Online Scholarship Form](https://app.racereach.com/form/71734)

evidence.excerpt:
Michael Kuchenbrod Memorial Scholarship
Criteria for first year applicant:
Whitefish High School graduate
Minimum 2.5 GPA from high school
Attend a 2-yr, 4-yr, or vocational/trade post-secondary institution in Montana full time (12 credit minimum per semester)
Renewable criteria
Awardees from year 1 are eligible for renewal for up to 3 additional years
The student must contact the Kuchenbrod family in writing with any or all of the following information once per year:
Current major, GPA, courses that have sparked interest/been rewarding or challenging, college life experiences or updates
The student must contact Whitefish Education Foundation and provide the following:
Transcript from year 2-4 with evidence a 2.5 minimum cumulative GPA
Evidence of 12 credit minimum schedule for years 2-4
Application elements:
Personal essay approximately 500 words/one page.
Describe your plans for the future, including your educational, career, and personal goals.  What inspired your goals, and how do you plan to achieve them?  Explain how receiving this scholarship will support your journey and help you make a positive impact in your community and/or chosen field.  Include specific details about your intended major, career path, or areas of passion and interest.  Discuss any role models, experiences, or events that shaped your future goals.
At least one letter of recommendation (no more than 2) from any adult other than a relative that knows the applicant well.
One page resume
Official high school transcript
Calculated SAI from your FAFSA
Acceptance letter from a Montana post secondary institution
Submit all of the above to [school contact omitted] by the end of May 7th, 2026.
Amount and follow up action
One $5000 award each year to a new WHS graduate
Each recipient may renew (for $5000) each year up through their 4th year of post-secondary education
Checks for each award will be written to the institution in the student’s name after all documents (letter of acceptance and registration of classes) have been submitted to WEF.

evidence.excerpt:
Michael Kuchenbrod Memorial Scholarship
Criteria for first year applicant:
Whitefish High School graduate
Minimum 2.5 GPA from high school
Attend a 2-yr, 4-yr, or vocational/trade post-secondary institution in Montana full time (12 credit minimum per semester)
Renewable criteria
Awardees from year 1 are eligible for renewal for up to 3 additional years
The student must contact the Kuchenbrod family in writing with any or all of the following information once per year:
Current major, GPA, courses that have sparked interest/been rewarding or challenging, college life experiences or updates
The student must contact Whitefish Education Foundation and provide the following:
Transcript from year 2-4 with evidence a 2.5 minimum cumulative GPA
Evidence of 12 credit minimum schedule for years 2-4
Application elements:
Personal essay approximately 500 words/one page.
Describe your plans for the future, including your educational, career, and personal goals.  What inspired your goals, and how do you plan to achieve them?  Explain how receiving this scholarship will support your journey and help you make a positive impact in your community and/or chosen field.  Include specific details about your intended major, career path, or areas of passion and interest.  Discuss any role models, experiences, or events that shaped your future goals.
At least one letter of recommendation (no more than 2) from any adult other than a relative that knows the applicant well.
One page resume
Official high school transcript
Calculated SAI from your FAFSA
Acceptance letter from a Montana post secondary institution
Submit all of the above to [school contact omitted] by the end of May 7th, 2026.
Amount and follow up action
One $5000 award each year to a new WHS graduate
Each recipient may renew (for $5000) each year up through their 4th year of post-secondary education
Checks for each award will be written to the institution in the student’s name after all documents (letter of acceptance and registration of classes) have been submitted to WEF.

## Our Commitment

The Latino Professionals in Aerospace (LPA) is committed to our community by providing opportunities in aviation. LPA has established key partnerships with both aviation and non-aviation related organizations and companies that allow us to make scholarships available to a diverse group of recipients. These scholarships help recipients further their careers in aviation related fields.


$3.2M+

## General Eligibility

All applicants must meet these requirements. Some scholarships have additional criteria.

1

#### Active LPA Member

Must be an active LPA member (Student, Standard, or Lifetime tier).

2

#### Age Requirement

Must be at least 17 years old. United Aviate Academy requires 18+.

3

#### U.S. Based Training

Must be enrolled or accepted to an accredited institution within the United States or its territories.

4

#### Direct to Institution

Scholarship amounts vary. All funds are sent directly to the certified educational institution.

## What You Need to Apply

Prepare these items before starting your application.

📄

#### Current Resume

One-page limit. Education, work history, volunteer experience, and honors.

👥

#### Two Recommendations

From professors, employers, or mentors. One page each. LPA members preferred.

✎️

#### Two Essays

500-word limit each. Showcase your passion and alignment with LPA's mission.

✅

#### Enrollment Verification

Proof of enrollment or acceptance. Required upon awarding of scholarship.
